root_idea.summary: Forceful contact directed at another body: striking with the whole hand, thrusting or piercing, and pushing.
root_idea.development: The lexical range differentiates forceful contact by its manner or effect, extending from a hand-blow to a spear-thrust, push, and related agentive or resultative uses.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form I perfect citation form وَكَزَ.

senses.definition: To strike or beat forcefully; in the Quranic occurrence, to deliver a blow with the hand or fist.
senses.usage_conditions: The object is a person in 28:15, where Moses delivers the blow. The broader striking sense is not restricted to a particular object or instrument.

senses.definition: To thrust or pierce forcefully, including with a spear.
senses.usage_conditions: This forceful-thrusting value is included in the Quran-focused lexical range, although the supplied contextual gloss for the sole occurrence identifies a hand-blow rather than separately disambiguating a spear-thrust.
This pushing or repelling value is included in the Quran-focused lexical range, though the supplied contextual gloss for the sole occurrence reflects the striking sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To break someone's nose by a forceful blow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A resultative specialization of striking, recorded as a distinct Classical Arabic use.
A conventional use describing incitement or urging.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who strikes or beats much with his fist.
Standing ready or prepared for a thing or affair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Occurs in the expression مُتَوَكِّزٌ بِأَمْرٍ.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Breaking the nose as a result of a blow.

cautions: The sole QAC occurrence is 28:15 and its supplied contextual gloss is a fist-strike. The Quran-focused lexical entry lists thrusting and pushing alongside hand-striking but does not separately assign those values to that verse.
The preparedness meaning of مُتَوَكِّزٌ بِأَمْرٍ is retained as a supplied Classical entry, but it is not projected into the Quranic meanings of وَكَزَ.
